finding: With both presence and game-activity callbacks enabled, addClient and removeClient reserved the game ticket first but submitted the presence ticket first. Dispatcher admission waits for the predecessor's submitted signal, so registration/removal blocked before ready or subsequent Hub work.
change: Reserve presence before game activity consistently with submission order, on first/additional connection and last/partial removal. No authentication, visibility or ready-payload guard was weakened.
verification: Final complete server go test ./... passed. After restarting the isolated local QA backend, both actual browser clients received ready; the banner cleared and server navigation restored. Reloading B after the removal fix left A connected and B reconnected successfully.
New first/additional registration regression failed before the fix in both cases with a bounded one-second acknowledgement timeout, then passed after the ordering change.
New last/partial removal regression failed before the follow-on fix in both cases with a bounded one-second completion timeout, then passed after the ordering change.
Registration, removal, lifecycle and callback-dispatcher tests passed five repeats.
Final complete websocket package: go test ./ws -count=1 -timeout=120s passed in 5.766s.
A separate real-store client ready-wiring test passed, with scoped ESLint and TypeScript passing; only background HTTP is mocked in that test.
remaining: This does not establish complete voice/device/network-recovery acceptance or release readiness.
release: No commit, push, merge, production migration, deployment or publication.
